item.title: Run threaded host kernels
item.description:
Split one particle movement call into chunks that run concurrently on host worker threads. Use this when a single kernel call covers many independent rows and profiling shows that the call dominates a step. Only the rows of one call are split; systems still run one after another in registration order. Threaded execution is experimental.

Start with Update entities with systems and kernels.

Move particles in threaded chunks

The stage uses the portable particle model and the movement kernel from the first simulation.

@fieldwise_init
struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic."""

    var x: Float32
    var y: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time."""

    var dx: Float32
    var dy: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Time(Copyable, Movable):
    """Shared simulated step length."""

    var delta: Float32
comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]()
comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]()


def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]):
    """Moves each row using its velocity and the shared step length.

    Args:
        context: Matching rows and read-only time.
    """
    ref time = context.resources.get[Time]()
    for particle in context:
        ref position = particle.get[Position]()
        ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]()
        position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta
        position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta

move is a thin kernel: a named def function that run receives as a compile-time parameter, as in context.run[move](). It captures no local variables and declares no capture slots; threaded execution requires both. Each row writes only its own Position, so no two chunks write the same data. Resources().read[Time]() declares Time read-only, so all chunks share one immutable value.

Opt in for one call with threaded=True:

@fieldwise_init
struct Move[threaded: Bool](System):
    """Opts into host chunks for this movement kernel."""

    def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises:
        """Moves disjoint rows and joins before returning.

        Args:
            context: Access to the simulation world.

        Raises:
            Error: If threaded eligibility or preparation fails.
        """
        context.run[move, threaded=Self.threaded]()

Then give the world more than one worker:

def run_stage[threaded: Bool](workers: Int) raises -> Position:
    """Checks parallel dispatch and whole-range fallback against exact values.

    Parameters:
        threaded: Whether to opt into the threaded engine.

    Args:
        workers: Submitted task budget; one exercises sequential fallback.

    Raises:
        Error: If configuration, execution, or a result check fails.

    Returns:
        Coordinate sums after two steps.
    """
    var world = World[Position, Velocity](
        execution_config=ThreadedExecutionConfig(
            workers=workers, chunks_per_worker=2, min_parallel_rows=0
        )
    )
    world.resources.add(Time(0.25))
    _ = world.storage.add_entities(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 2), count=4097)
    var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity](world^)
    scheduler.add_system(Move[threaded]())
    scheduler.run(steps=2)
    var total = Position(0, 0)
    for particle in scheduler.world.storage.query[move_filter]():
        ref position = particle.get[Position]()
        assert_almost_equal(position.x, 0.5)
        assert_almost_equal(position.y, 1.0)
        total.x += position.x
        total.y += position.y
    return total


def main() raises:
    """Compares the sequential, one-worker, and multi-task call paths.

    Raises:
        Error: If an execution path disagrees.
    """
    var sequential = run_stage[False](1)
    var fallback = run_stage[True](1)
    var threaded = run_stage[True](4)
    assert_equal(fallback.x, sequential.x)
    assert_equal(fallback.y, sequential.y)
    assert_equal(threaded.x, sequential.x)
    assert_equal(threaded.y, sequential.y)
    print(
        "PASS: sequential, one-worker fallback, and four-task particle parity"
    )

ThreadedExecutionConfig sets the number of tasks Larecs submits per call, not reserved cores. chunks_per_worker=2 targets two chunks per worker, and min_parallel_rows=0 removes the row cutoff, so the 4097 particles split into chunks. The driver runs the same two steps three times, each in a fresh world: sequentially, threaded with one worker, and threaded with four workers.

From the repository root, run:

pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/threaded.mojo

The program prints a PASS line when all three runs move every particle to (0.5, 1.0).

How Larecs splits the rows

Larecs splits each matching physical store into kernel chunks: contiguous row ranges, each passed to one kernel invocation. Workers claim chunks in an unspecified order, and run returns only after every chunk has finished. This changes what code outside the row loop sees:

  • Code before or after the for loop runs once per chunk, not once per store.
  • A row’s idx restarts at zero in each chunk; row indices are not entity IDs.
  • Work that reads rows of other chunks needs a later run, after this call returns.

Work mapping explains how Larecs sizes chunks.

Variations

Keep small calls sequential

The default configuration has one worker, four chunks per worker, and a cutoff of 65,536 matched rows. With one worker, or with fewer matched rows than min_parallel_rows, a threaded=True call runs sequentially, once per physical store or selected range. Keep threaded=True in the system and set the worker budget per world; the compile-time eligibility checks apply either way.

Run threaded on a selection

EntitySelection.run accepts the same threaded=True parameter and splits only the selection’s rows.

Read an owning collection

Ordinary resources in a threaded call must be read-only values without pointers or owned memory. To read a list or buffer, wrap it in a portable resource.

Failures and limits

Failure Cause and fix
Threaded components require pointer-free trivial plain values An accessed component holds a pointer or owns memory, such as a List. Remove it from the filter, or keep that data in a portable resource.
Threaded resources require pointer-free plain values or DevicePassableResource adapters A read resource owns memory or holds a pointer. Use a portable resource.
Threaded resources require explicit read access The kernel declares an ordinary resource as writable, including through the Resources[Time]() read-write default. Declare it with read, or write per-row output as in Coordinate shared writes.
Compile error for a lexical closure, captures, or DEVICE Threaded execution requires a thin kernel without capture slots on ExecutionBackend.HOST.
ThreadedExecutionConfig raises workers and chunks_per_worker must be positive, their product must fit in an Int, and min_parallel_rows must not be negative.
Structural lock exhaustion Each threaded call adds one structural lock to those already held, even when it runs sequentially. Live queries and selections, even empty ones, hold the others; end those you no longer need.
No speedup Dispatch costs time; measure complete steps before you change the cutoff.

Chunks are independent only in the rows they visit. Structural locks are not mutexes: shared state still needs a race-free write strategy. The threaded execution reference lists the remaining lock, alias, and failure rules.

Complete program

item.title: Execute on a device
item.description:
Run the particle movement kernel on an accelerator, such as a GPU, and check that it produces the same positions as the host. Use this when a kernel does enough arithmetic per particle to outweigh copying data to the device and back. Device execution is experimental; it needs the repository’s pinned Mojo and MAX environment and a supported accelerator.

Start with Update entities with systems and kernels and Share time and configuration.

Select the device in the system

The stage uses the portable particle model, whose components Larecs can copy to the device byte by byte.

@fieldwise_init
struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic."""

    var x: Float32
    var y: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time."""

    var dx: Float32
    var dy: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Time(Copyable, Movable):
    """Shared simulated step length."""

    var delta: Float32

The kernel is the movement kernel from the first simulation, unchanged.

comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]()
comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]()


def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]):
    """Moves each row using its velocity and the shared step length.

    Args:
        context: Matching rows and read-only time.
    """
    ref time = context.resources.get[Time]()
    for particle in context:
        ref position = particle.get[Position]()
        ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]()
        position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta
        position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta

move is a thin kernel, the only kind of kernel device execution accepts. The system chooses the target with the backend parameter of SystemContext.run:

@fieldwise_init
struct Move[backend: ExecutionBackend](System):
    """Selects the execution target explicitly."""

    def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises:
        """Runs one synchronous movement step.

        Args:
            context: Access to this simulation's world.

        Raises:
            Error: If resource preparation or execution fails.
        """
        context.run[move, backend=Self.backend]()

Move[ExecutionBackend.DEVICE]() runs move on the device, and Move[ExecutionBackend.HOST]() runs it sequentially on the host, which is also the default when you omit backend. The ExecutionBackend value is a compile-time parameter, so each system specialization runs on one target.

Let the filter decide what moves

Larecs copies only the data the kernel declares. For each call, it packs the matching rows of every physical store into contiguous device columns, runs the kernel once over all of them, and copies written columns back to their original rows.

Scroll horizontally to read the full figure.

Access declarations determine transfer directions.

Declaration Upload before the kernel Copy back after the kernel
include[Position]() Yes Yes
read[Velocity](), Resources().read[Time]() Yes No
write[T]() No; the kernel must set every row it visits Yes

run returns after the kernel finishes and Larecs has copied every written component, read-write resource, and mutable capture back to the host. The next system sees the new values on the host. Rows that the filter does not match stay untouched.

Compare the device with the host

The driver runs two steps on 37 moving particles and one unmatched marker, once per target, each in a fresh world.

def run_stage[backend: ExecutionBackend]() raises -> Position:
    """Runs two steps and checks both coordinates and an unmatched marker.

    Parameters:
        backend: Explicit target for this independent simulation.

    Raises:
        Error: If setup, execution, or a position check fails.

    Returns:
        The sum of the moving particles' final coordinates.
    """
    var world = World[Position, Velocity]()
    world.resources.add(Time(0.25))
    _ = world.storage.add_entities(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 2), count=37)
    var marker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(-3, -3))
    var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity](world^)
    scheduler.add_system(Move[backend]())
    scheduler.run(steps=2)
    var total = Position(0, 0)
    for particle in scheduler.world.storage.query[move_filter]():
        ref position = particle.get[Position]()
        assert_almost_equal(position.x, 0.5)
        assert_almost_equal(position.y, 1.0)
        total.x += position.x
        total.y += position.y
    assert_equal(scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](marker).x, -3)
    return total


def main() raises:
    """Reports device execution separately from a hardware skip.

    Raises:
        Error: If host checks, device execution, or parity checks fail.
    """
    var host = run_stage[ExecutionBackend.HOST]()
    assert_almost_equal(host.x, 18.5)
    assert_almost_equal(host.y, 37.0)
    print("PASS: host particle checks")
    comptime if has_accelerator():
        var device = run_stage[ExecutionBackend.DEVICE]()
        assert_almost_equal(device.x, host.x)
        assert_almost_equal(device.y, host.y)
        print("PASS: actual device execution and host/device parity")
    else:
        # A skip is an application choice; DEVICE itself never falls back.
        var empty = World[Position, Velocity]()
        empty.resources.add(Time(0.25))
        var context = SystemContext(empty)
        with assert_raises():
            context.run[move, backend=ExecutionBackend.DEVICE]()
        print("SKIP: device parity (no accelerator compilation support)")

Every mover ends at (0.5, 1.0), the marker stays at (-3, -3), and the device sums match the host sums. has_accelerator() decides whether the program attempts the device at all; without support, it checks that a device call raises instead of falling back.

From the repository root, run:

pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/device.mojo

A PASS line for the device means the kernel ran on the accelerator and matched the host; a SKIP line means this machine has no supported accelerator and only the host ran.

How device threads visit rows

On the host, a kernel invocation covers one physical store or one threaded chunk. On a device, one launch covers all packed rows, and each device thread runs the kernel body. The for loop over the context uses grid-stride iteration: each thread starts at its global thread index and advances by the total number of launched threads, so every row is visited exactly once, even when there are more rows than threads.

Scroll horizontally to read the full figure.

One row loop, three invocation mappings.

Code outside the for loop runs once per device thread. A row’s idx is its offset in the packed rows, and row indices are not entity IDs.

Variations

Choose the target at run time

The backend is a compile-time parameter. To choose at run time, branch and call each specialization explicitly, for example add Move[ExecutionBackend.DEVICE]() when has_accelerator() is true and Move[ExecutionBackend.HOST]() otherwise. Larecs itself has no device fallback.

Run on a selection

EntitySelection.run accepts the same backend parameter and packs only the selection’s rows.

Pass local values or owning data

Use explicit capture slots for a step-local value and portable resources for an owning collection.

Skip unchanged uploads

By default, every device call uploads all readable columns and resources. Reuse unchanged device copies skips uploads of data that has not changed since the last call.

Failures and limits

Failure Cause and fix
run raises that DEVICE requires accelerator support or a working device context No usable accelerator. Fix the accelerator or toolchain, or select ExecutionBackend.HOST; there is no device fallback.
Compile error: every accessed component type must be device-safe Make the component TrivialRegisterPassable, as in the portable model. Only accessed components are checked.
Compile error: device resources require pointer-free trivial plain values The resource owns memory or holds a pointer. Use a portable resource for owning data.
Compile error: device write-only resources are unsupported Declare an ordinary device resource with read or read_write.
Compile error for a lexical closure or threaded=True Device execution needs a thin kernel and cannot be combined with threaded host execution.
run raises about a missing resource, even with no matching rows Add every declared resource during setup.

A failed device call does not roll back host writes that already happened. The device execution reference covers empty matches, transfer and synchronization failures, and when a world rejects further device work. Transfers and preparation can dominate a small kernel; measure complete simulation steps before choosing a backend.

item.title: Pass local values to kernels
item.description:
Give the particle kernel a step-local scale and get a particle count back, without storing either value as a world resource. Use a lexical closure when the kernel runs sequentially on the host, and explicit capture slots when the same kernel must also run on a device. Threaded execution accepts neither; pass its inputs through read-only resources or components.

Start with Execute on a device, which introduces the backend parameter. Run threaded host kernels defines thin kernels.

Borrow locals with a closure on the host

Both programs on this page use the portable particle model.

@fieldwise_init
struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic."""

    var x: Float32
    var y: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time."""

    var dx: Float32
    var dy: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Time(Copyable, Movable):
    """Shared simulated step length."""

    var delta: Float32

A lexical closure is a def nested inside another function that names the local variables it uses in a capture list. Here, move is defined inside Move.update and passed to run as a value:

@fieldwise_init
struct Move(System):
    """Counts particles through a sequential host closure."""

    def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises:
        """Moves the particles and observes a synchronous captured result.

        Args:
            context: Access to the particle world.

        Raises:
            Error: If resources, execution, or the visit check fail.
        """
        var scale: Float32 = 2
        var visits = 0

        def move(
            rows: KernelContext[
                Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity](),
                Resources().read[Time](),
            ]
        ) {imm scale, mut visits}:
            """Moves each row and counts it through a host borrow.

            Args:
                rows: One matching physical store's rows and time.
            """
            ref time = rows.resources.get[Time]()
            for particle in rows:
                ref position = particle.get[Position]()
                ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]()
                position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta * scale
                position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta * scale
                visits += 1

        context.run(move)
        assert_equal(visits, 2)

The capture list {imm scale, mut visits} borrows scale read-only and visits mutably. context.run(move) selects the overload that takes a callable value; it runs only sequentially on the host. Larecs calls move once per matching physical store, and visits increases once per row. run returns after the last call, so the assertion sees the final count.

The driver puts the two particles into different physical stores:

def main() raises:
    """Checks the closure across two matching physical stores.

    Raises:
        Error: If setup, execution, or a position check fails.
    """
    var world = World[Position, Velocity, Int32]()
    world.resources.add(Time(0.25))
    var walker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 0))
    var climber = world.storage.add_entity(
        Position(5, 0), Velocity(0, 2), Int32(1)
    )
    var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity, Int32](world^)
    scheduler.add_system(Move())
    scheduler.run(steps=1)
    assert_almost_equal(scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](walker).x, 0.5)
    assert_almost_equal(scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](climber).y, 1.0)
    print("PASS: lexical host captures across two stores")

The extra Int32 component gives climber a different composition and therefore its own physical store; it does not change which entities move matches. Both particles move once, and visits counts rows across both calls.

From the repository root, run:

pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/lexical_closure.mojo

Declare explicit slots for a thin kernel

A thin kernel cannot borrow locals, but it can declare ordered capture slots with Captures. The system binds a local value to each slot when it calls run, on the host or on a device.

comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]()
comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]()
comptime locals_spec = Captures[ReadCapture[Float32], MutCapture[Int32]]()


def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources, locals_spec]):
    """Moves particles and records the processed count with a single writer.

    Args:
        context: Rows, time, and ordered scale/count capture slots.
    """
    ref time = context.resources.get[Time]()
    var scale = context.captures.get[0]()
    for particle in context:
        ref position = particle.get[Position]()
        ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]()
        position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta * scale
        position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta * scale
    # The count is shared, not one private scalar per device thread.
    comptime if is_gpu():
        if global_idx.x != 0:
            return
    context.captures.get[1]() += context.length

Slot 0 is a ReadCapture input; get[0]() returns its value. Slot 1 is a MutCapture output. Every invocation, and on a device every thread, sees the same output value, so only one writer may update it:

  • On the host, each invocation covers one physical store and adds its own row count, context.length. Sequential invocations never overlap.
  • On a device, one launch covers all rows. comptime if is_gpu() compiles the check only for the device, where only the thread with global index zero adds the packed row count.

This works because no thread reads another thread’s result. A thread-zero branch is not a barrier, and it does not make a general reduction safe.

Bind locals in the declared order when the system runs:

struct Move[backend: ExecutionBackend](System):
    """Binds local values for one synchronous step."""

    def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises:
        """Checks count copy-back before the system returns.

        Args:
            context: Access to the simulation world.

        Raises:
            Error: If binding, execution, or the count check fails.
        """
        var scale: Float32 = 2
        var processed: Int32 = 0
        context.run[move, backend=Self.backend](
            read_capture(scale), mut_capture(processed)
        )

        assert_equal(processed, 37)

read_capture and mut_capture borrow scale and processed until run returns. On the host, the kernel uses the original values. On a device, Larecs uploads every binding on each call and copies the mutable slot back before run returns, so processed holds 37 at the assertion.

From the repository root, run:

pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/captures.mojo

A PASS line for the device means the slots were bound, executed, and copied back on the accelerator; a SKIP line means only the host ran.

Variations

Keep a value between steps

A capture lives for one run call. A value that persists between steps, or that owns memory, belongs in a resource or a portable resource.

Produce one result per particle

When many invocations or threads contribute to a result, write a per-particle component and reduce it after run, as in Coordinate shared writes.

Failures and limits

Failure Cause and fix
Compile error on the slot count, type, or mutability Bind one value per slot in declaration order, with the declared type. Two slots may share a type; their index distinguishes them.
Borrow-checker error on one local One local cannot be bound read-only and mutably in the same call. Use separate values.
Compile error for a device capture that owns memory or holds a pointer Device captures copy plain bytes. Use a portable resource for owning data.
Wrong result from several writers A mutable slot provides no synchronization. Use one writer, or per-particle output.
Compile error for a closure with DEVICE or threaded=True Lexical closures run only sequentially on the host. Use explicit slots for a device.

Keep references from capture slots and closure borrows inside the kernel; they must not outlive the call. The capture reference lists the remaining binding rules.

item.title: Use portable resources
item.description:
Read an owning collection, such as a list of samples, from the particle kernel on both the host and a device. An ordinary resource that owns memory works on the sequential host only, because Larecs cannot copy its heap data to a device byte by byte. A portable resource is a resource source with an adapter. It keeps the owner on the host and gives each kernel a kernel view, a plain value that points to the data on the kernel’s target.

Start with Share values with resources and Execute on a device. Mutable portable resources are experimental; this page uses read-only views.

Separate the owner from the kernel view

The particle types follow the portable particle model, and Time stays an ordinary read-only resource.

@fieldwise_init
struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic."""

    var x: Float32
    var y: Float32

    var dx: Float32
    var dy: Float32


@fieldwise_init

    """Shared simulated step length."""

    var delta: Float32

The stage adds two resource sources, the owning values stored in the world:

comptime Samples = BufferResource[DType.float32]


@fieldwise_init
struct Grid(DevicePassableResource):
    """Owns samples and dimensions on the host."""

    comptime Adapter = GridAdapter
    var values: List[Float32]
    var width: Int
    var height: Int


@fieldwise_init
struct GridView(TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Borrows immutable samples in the current target's address space."""

    var values: Pointer[Float32, ImmUntrackedOrigin]
    var width: Int
    var height: Int

    def last(self) -> Float32:
        """Reads the final sample of a validated nonempty grid.

        Returns:
            The bottom-right sample.
        """
        return self.values[unsafe_offset=self.width * self.height - 1]

Samples is a BufferResource, the built-in source for a contiguous buffer of scalars. Its kernel view is ReadBuffer, which has a length and bounds-checked indexing. Grid is a custom DevicePassableResource: it owns a List and names the adapter that creates its view, GridView. GridView holds a pointer to the samples and the grid’s dimensions, and last() reads the final sample. The pointer is target-local: it refers to host memory in a host run and to device memory in a device run.

Prepare the view for each target

A ResourceAdapter checks the current owner and builds the view for the target of each call.

struct GridAdapter(ResourceAdapter):
    """Prepares the same immutable descriptor for either target."""

    comptime Source = Grid
    comptime View[mut: Bool] = GridView

    @staticmethod
    def validate(source: Self.Source) raises:
        """Validates shape and bounds before either target is prepared.

        Args:
            source: Current host owner.

        Raises:
            Error: If shape arithmetic overflows or sample counts disagree.
        """
        if source.width <= 0 or source.height <= 0:
            raise Error("Grid dimensions must be positive")
        if source.width > Int(Int64.MAX) // source.height:
            raise Error("Grid dimensions overflow")
        if source.width * source.height != len(source.values):
            raise Error("Grid shape must match sample count")

    @staticmethod
    def bind_host(source: Self.Source) raises -> Self.View[False]:
        """Borrows the validated owner's samples without copying.

        Args:
            source: Owner retained through invocation completion.

        Returns:
            Host-local immutable descriptor.
        """
        return {
            Pointer[Float32, ImmUntrackedOrigin](
                unsafe_from_address=Int(source.values.unsafe_ptr())
            ),
            source.width,
            source.height,
        }

    @staticmethod
    def prepare_device(
        source: Self.Source, mut cache: ResourceDeviceCache
    ) raises -> Self.View[False]:
        """Uploads samples through invocation-owned staging.

        Args:
            source: Current validated owner.
            cache: Source-type and device-context local allocations.

        Raises:
            Error: If allocation or upload fails.

        Returns:
            Descriptor containing a device-local sample pointer.
        """
        return {
            cache.upload[Float32](0, Span(source.values)),
            source.width,
            source.height,
        }
  • validate runs before every call, including calls that match no entities. It rejects empty or inconsistent grids, so last() never reads out of bounds.
  • bind_host points the view at the owner’s own list; it copies nothing.
  • prepare_device uploads the samples through ResourceDeviceCache slot 0 and returns a view that points to device memory. The cache keeps the device allocation between calls; by default, the samples upload again on every call.

Request the source type in the kernel

The kernel declares and looks up resources by their source type:

comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time, Samples, Grid]()


def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]):
    """Uses source-type lookup to read two portable views.

    ref grid = context.resources.get[Grid]()
    ref time = context.resources.get[Time]()

A PASS line for the device means the kernel read both views on the accelerator; a SKIP line means only the host ran.

Keep sources and views valid during a call

For the duration of a call, Larecs holds a lease on every bound source: it keeps the source alive and in place, and looking it up, replacing it, or removing it from inside the call raises. Two rules keep views valid:

  • Keep views, their pointers, and references obtained from them inside the kernel invocation.
  • Do not change, resize, or free the owner through a reference you kept from before the call while the call runs.

A lease protects the source’s lifetime; it does not synchronize threads. Structural locks are not mutexes, and neither are leases. The adapter reference lists the remaining rules for adapter authors.

Variations

Write through an adapter

GridAdapter supports reading only, so declare its source with read; the Resources[Grid]() default means read-write and fails to compile. An adapter that sets supports_mutation can provide a writable view for sequential host calls, and one that also sets supports_concurrent_mutation can provide it for threaded and device calls. The mutable adapter reference and the scatter example show the hooks and an atomic slot reservation. For most shared output, prefer per-particle results.

Skip unchanged uploads

With device-copy reuse enabled, a read-only source that has not changed since the last device call skips prepare_device and reuses its view.

Failure Cause and fix

Compile error: mutable access requires Adapter.supports_mutation The source is declared writable. Declare it with read, or implement a writer view.
Crash or wrong values from a view pointer The view points to memory that does not belong to the owner or the device cache, or an earlier reference changed the owner during the call. Return owner-backed or cache-backed memory only.
Stale samples with copy reuse enabled The owner changed through a reference that Larecs does not track. Reacquire it with get after each run, or invalidate it.

item.title: Reuse unchanged device copies
item.description:
Skip uploading particle data that has not changed since the last device call. Use this after the kernel already passes the host and device comparison and a measurement shows that uploads matter. Reuse is off by default, set per world, and experimental. Written outputs still copy back to the host after every call.

With reuse enabled, a device call uploads a resource or column only when the revision of its device copy, the bytes already on the device, differs from the current one. In the sequence:

  • read calls leave the revisions unchanged, so the second step reuses every input.
  • get through mutable storage advances the revision whether or not you write, so the step after get[Time]().delta = 0.5 uploads Time again.
  • A successful device call leaves the written Position current on both sides, so the next call can skip its upload too.

Retained capacity does not prove that its contents are current.

Larecs keeps device allocations between calls whether or not reuse is enabled; a kept allocation says nothing about whether its bytes are current. With reuse enabled, a read-only portable resource whose source is current skips prepare_device and reuses its view.

Larecs advances a revision when you call get, not when you later write through the reference it returned. item.title: Coordinate shared writes
item.description:
Compute one shared result, the total displacement of all particles, without a data race. Each particle writes its own output in the kernel, and one caller sums the outputs after run returns. This works on every target, including threaded chunks and device threads, where many invocations run at once. For data you own outside the world, Larecs also provides standalone atomic values and guarded values.

Start with Update entities with systems and kernels. Larecs does not bind synchronization primitives to kernels automatically; see compatibility and status.

Write a separate output for each particle

The stage uses the portable particle model and adds a Displacement component that belongs to each particle.

@fieldwise_init
struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic."""

    var x: Float32
    var y: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time."""

    var dx: Float32
    var dy: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Time(Copyable, Movable):
    """Shared simulated step length."""

    var delta: Float32
@fieldwise_init
struct Displacement(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """A private output for one particle, avoiding a shared kernel counter."""

    var x: Float32
    var y: Float32


comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]().write[
    Displacement
]()
comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]()


def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]):
    """Writes every per-row output before a later single-caller reduction.

    Args:
        context: Particle inputs and set-only displacement output.
    """
    ref time = context.resources.get[Time]()
    for particle in context:
        ref position = particle.get[Position]()
        ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]()
        var dx = velocity.dx * time.delta
        var dy = velocity.dy * time.delta
        position.x += dx
        position.y += dy
        particle.set(Displacement(dx, dy))

write[Displacement]() grants set-only access, so the kernel must set the output on every row it visits. No two rows share an output, so the kernel needs no synchronization on any target. A resource or a mutable capture slot, by contrast, is one value that every invocation would write.

Reduce after the kernel returns

The system sums the outputs once run has returned:

@fieldwise_init
struct Move(System):
    """Runs row work before a single-caller reduction."""

    def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises:
        """Reduces completed per-row outputs without a shared kernel write.

        Args:
            context: Access to the world after synchronous kernel completion.

        Raises:
            Error: If execution or the reduction check fails.
        """
        context.run[move]()
        var total = Displacement(0, 0)
        for particle in context.world[].storage.query[
            Filter().read[Displacement]()
        ]():
            ref value = particle.get[Displacement]()
            total.x += value.x
            total.y += value.y
        assert_almost_equal(total.x, 9.25)
        assert_almost_equal(total.y, 18.5)

Variations

Reduce in several passes

For a parallel reduction, write partial results to disjoint per-particle or per-group components, then combine them in a later run or on the host. Each pass reads only output that an earlier, finished call wrote.

Use a single writer

One designated writer may update a shared value when it does not need other threads’ unfinished results, as the capture count does with global thread zero. A thread-zero branch is not a barrier.

Update data you own with atomic or guarded values

These primitives work on storage you own, outside the world:

def check_primitives() raises:
    """Checks target-local host primitives independently of ECS bindings.

    Raises:
        Error: If an atomic or guard check fails.
    """
    var counter = AtomicValue[UInt32](0)
    var updates = counter.write_view()
    assert_equal(updates.fetch_add(1), UInt32(0))
    var result = updates.compare_exchange(1, 5)
    assert_true(result.exchanged)
    assert_equal(result.observed, UInt32(1))
    updates.store[Ordering.RELEASE](7)
    assert_equal(updates.load[Ordering.ACQUIRE](), UInt32(7))

    var state = Synchronized[UInt32](10)
    var access = state.write_view()
    var attempt = access.try_read()
    assert_true(attempt.is_acquired())
    var reader = attempt^.take()
    assert_equal(reader.value(), UInt32(10))
    assert_false(access.try_write().is_acquired())
    reader^.release()
    var write_attempt = access.try_write()
    assert_true(write_attempt.is_acquired())
    var writer = write_attempt^.take()
    writer.value() += 5
    writer^.release()
    var read_attempt = access.try_read()
    assert_true(read_attempt.is_acquired())
    var after = read_attempt^.take()
    assert_equal(after.value(), UInt32(15))
  • AtomicValue owns a UInt32 or Int32 scalar, and AtomicView borrows it. fetch_add returns the previous value. compare_exchange reports whether it exchanged and which value it observed. Operations use relaxed ordering unless you pass an ordering, such as store[Ordering.RELEASE] and load[Ordering.ACQUIRE], at compile time.
  • Synchronized owns guarded data, and SyncView borrows it. try_read and try_write make one attempt and never wait. Check is_acquired before you consume the attempt with take. Several readers may hold the value at once; a writer excludes everyone else. The guard releases at scope exit or through release.

A false is_acquired means Busy: the single attempt met a conflicting guard, a state that changed during the attempt, or the maximum reader count. Larecs does not retry. Record the unfinished work for a later pass, or skip the update only if your application can lose it.

Failures and limits

Failure Cause and fix
Wrong totals from a shared resource or capture Several invocations wrote one value. Write per-particle output and reduce after run.
try_read or try_write returns Busy The attempt met a conflicting guard, a concurrently changed state, or the reader limit. Do not spin; defer the work to a later pass.
Compile error for an ordering, compare-exchange, or guard on an Apple GPU Apple devices support only relaxed or acquire loads, relaxed or release stores, and relaxed add and subtract. Use per-particle output instead.
Compile error when an AtomicView or SyncView is in a resource or capture Views do not transfer to kernels. Use per-particle output, or a mutable adapter that manages its own atomic buffer.
Ordinary data written next to a relaxed counter is not visible Relaxed operations order nothing else. Use release stores and acquire loads to publish data.

Structural locks are not mutexes; neither are resource leases. The synchronization reference lists supported orderings per backend, guard rules, and device memory requirements.
